questions.question: If 3 : 27 :: 5.6 : x and 5 : 35 :: 6 : y, then what is the ratio of x to y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Proportion 1: 3 → 27 (Scaling × 9) ∴ x = 5.6 × 9 = 50.4

Proportion 2: 5 → 35 (Scaling × 7) ∴ y = 6 × 7 = 42

Ratio x : y = 50.4 : 42

Simplify by 8.4: (50.4 ÷ 8.4) : (42 ÷ 8.4) = 6 : 5

**∴ Answer = 6 : 5**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Proportion 1: 3 : 27 :: 5.6 : x

Proportion 2: 5 : 35 :: 6 : y

**Formula used:**

Product of Extremes = Product of Means (If a : b :: c : d, then a × d = b × c)

 Proportion 1 (Finding x): 3 : 27 
 ×9 5.6 : x ⇒ x = 50.4 
• Proportion 2 (Finding y): 5 : 35 
 ×7 6 : y ⇒ y = 42 Final Ratio x : y = 6 : 5 

**Calculations:**

From 3 : 27 :: 5.6 : x

⇒ 3 × x = 27 × 5.6

⇒ x = (27 × 5.6) ÷ 3 = 9 × 5.6 = 50.4

From 5 : 35 :: 6 : y

⇒ 5 × y = 35 × 6

⇒ y = (35 × 6) ÷ 5 = 7 × 6 = 42

Ratio of x to y:

⇒ x : y = 50.4 : 42

⇒ x : y = 504 : 420

⇒ x : y = (504 ÷ 84) : (420 ÷ 84) = 6 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 5 (Option 4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

For a : b :: c : d, d is called the fourth proportional and is calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a : b :: b : c, then c is the third proportional to a and b, where c = b² ÷ a.

Compounded Ratio

The compounded ratio of two ratios (a : b) and (c : d) is given by (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.question: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, entrusted the Municipalities with ______ functional domains under the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **74th Constitutional Amendment Act**, passed in **1992**, provides a basic framework for decentralized governance in urban areas of **India**.
 
• This **Act** added a new **Twelfth Schedule** to the **Constitution of India**, which explicitly lists **18 functional items** or domains that are entrusted to **Municipalities**.
 
• These **18 functional domains** include **Urban planning** including town planning, **Regulation of land-use** and construction of buildings, and **Planning for economic and social development**.
 
• The schedule also mandates functions such as **Roads and bridges**, **Water supply** for domestic, industrial, and commercial purposes, **Public health**, **sanitation**, **conservancy**, and **solid waste management**.
 
• Other critical services listed are **Fire services**, **Urban forestry**, protection of the environment, and promotion of ecological aspects, alongside **Safeguarding the interests of weaker sections of society**, including the handicapped and mentally retarded.
 
• Additional domains involve **Slum improvement and up-gradation**, **Urban poverty alleviation**, and the provision of **urban amenities and facilities** such as parks, gardens, and playgrounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **74th Amendment Act** officially came into force on **June 1, 1993**, marking a significant milestone in **democratic decentralization**.
 
• It introduced **Part IX-A** to the **Constitution**, titled '**The Municipalities**', encompassing **Articles 243P to 243ZG**.
 
• The **Act** categorizes **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** into three types: **Nagar Panchayat** for areas in transition from rural to urban, **Municipal Council** for smaller urban areas, and **Municipal Corporation** for larger urban areas.
 
• Under **Article 243S**, the constitution of **Wards Committees** is required in municipalities having a population of **three lakhs or more**.
 
• To ensure financial viability, **Article 243I** and **243Y** mandate the **State Finance Commission** to review the financial position of **Municipalities** every **five years** and recommend the devolution of taxes and grants-in-aid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 243W** of the **Constitution** specifies the **powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities**, specifically empowering them to implement schemes for economic development and social justice as listed in the **Twelfth Schedule**.
 
• **Reservation of seats**: The **Act** provides mandatory reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes** and **Scheduled Tribes** in proportion to their population, and not less than **one-third** (33%) of the total seats must be reserved for **women**.
 
• The **duration** of a **Municipality** is fixed at **five years** from the date of its first meeting; if dissolved earlier, **elections** must be held within **six months**.
 
• The **State Election Commission**, constituted under **Article 243K**, is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the **Municipalities**.
 
• The **District Planning Committee (DPC)** is mandated under **Article 243ZD** to consolidate the plans prepared by **Panchayats** and **Municipalities** in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.

questions.question: Identify the tertiary activity from among the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Real estate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Economic activities** are broadly classified into three main sectors: **primary**, **secondary**, and **tertiary**. The **tertiary sector** is known as the **service sector** because it provides various services to consumers and other sectors rather than producing tangible goods.
 
• **Biotechnology** is an advanced field involving **Research and Development (R&D)** and the application of biological systems to create products. While it is related to industry, it is primarily classified as a **quaternary activity** due to its knowledge-based and specialized nature. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Real estate** involves services such as the **buying, selling, renting, and management of land and buildings**. Since it provides a commercial service to individuals and businesses, it is a classic example of a **tertiary activity**. ***Hence, statement B is correct.***
 
• The **Drink industry** (Beverage industry) involves the **processing and manufacturing** of raw materials into finished liquid products. Because it involves value addition through factory processes, it belongs to the **secondary sector**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• The **Construction industry** involves the physical creation of **infrastructure, roads, bridges, and buildings**. In economic terms, construction is categorized under the **secondary sector** because it involves the "fabrication" of physical structures. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tertiary Sector Characteristics:**

 
 
• This sector includes **trade, transport, communication, banking, insurance, and real estate**.
 
• In **India**, the tertiary sector is the largest contributor to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, accounting for approximately **53% to 55%** of the total **Gross Value Added (GVA)**.
 
• It plays a vital role in supporting the **primary (agriculture)** and **secondary (industrial)** sectors by facilitating the movement and sale of goods.
 
 
 
• **Primary Sector:**
 
 
• This sector involves the **extraction and harvesting of natural resources**.
 
• Key examples include **agriculture, forestry, fishing, mining, and quarrying**. In developing nations like India, a significant portion of the **workforce** is still employed in this sector.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector:**
 
 
• This sector focuses on the **manufacturing and processing** of raw materials into finished goods.
 
• It includes **large-scale industries** (like steel and automobiles), **small-scale units**, and the **construction** of physical assets.
 
 
 
• **Quaternary and Quinary Sectors:**
 
 
• The **Quaternary sector** is a subset of the tertiary sector, focusing on **information technology (IT)**, **consultancy**, and **scientific research**.
 
• The **Quinary sector** involves high-level **decision-making** by top executives, government officials, and researchers who influence global and national policies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real Estate in India:** The real estate sector is the **second-largest employer** in India after agriculture. It is expected to reach a market size of **$1 trillion** by the **year 2030**.
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** In India, the **Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA)** was enacted to protect the interests of homebuyers and boost investments in the sector.
 
• **Urbanization:** Rapid **urbanization** and the **Smart Cities Mission** have significantly fueled the growth of real estate and construction activities across the **country**.

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 26 hours respectively. A third tap can empty it in 26 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern, if all of them are opened together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency of filling tap (26 hours) and emptying tap (26 hours) cancel each other out.

Net filling is performed only by the first tap (4 hours).

Time to fill the full cistern = 4 hours.

Time to fill 1/4 of the cistern = 1/4 × 4 = 1 hour.

**∴ Answer = 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Time taken by Tap 1 (Fill) = 4 hours

Time taken by Tap 2 (Fill) = 26 hours

Time taken by Tap 3 (Empty) = 26 hours

**Formula used:**

Total Work = LCM of all given times

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Hours

 
 

 **Tap**
 **Number of Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Tap 1 (Fill)
 4
 52 units (LCM)
 +13
 
 

 Tap 2 (Fill)
 26
 +2
 
 

 Tap 3 (Empty)
 26
 −2
 
 

Combined Efficiency = 13 + 2 − 2 = 13 units/hour

Work to be completed (1/4 of total) = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 units

**Calculations:**

Total Capacity (LCM of 4 and 26) = 52 units

⇒ Efficiency of Tap 1 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13

⇒ Efficiency of Tap 2 = 52 ÷ 26 = 2

⇒ Efficiency of Tap 3 = −(52 ÷ 26) = −2

⇒ Net efficiency of all three taps = 13 + 2 − 2 = 13 units/hour

⇒ Time required to fill 1/4 of the cistern = 13 ÷ 13 = 1 hour

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Work in Pipes and Cisterns

Filling pipes are considered as positive work (+), while emptying or outlet pipes are considered as negative work (−).

Combined Rate Formula

If two pipes can fill a tank in x and y hours, the time taken to fill together is (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers of India forms a delta on the eastern coastal plains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Godavari** is the largest peninsular river system in **India** and is often referred to as the **Dakshina Ganga**. It flows eastward and forms a massive **delta** on the **eastern coastal plains** before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• Rivers like the **Godavari**, **Mahanadi**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri** flow towards the east because the **Deccan Plateau** has a general slope from west to east. These rivers carry large amounts of **alluvium** and sediment, which they deposit at their mouths, creating fertile **deltas**.
 
• In contrast, the **Narmada** and **Tapi** are major west-flowing rivers that originate in **Central India** and flow into the **Arabian Sea**. These rivers flow through narrow **rift valleys** and do not form deltas; instead, they form **estuaries**. *Hence, options A and D are incorrect.*
 
• The **Mahi** river also flows westwards, originating in **Madhya Pradesh** and passing through **Rajasthan** and **Gujarat** to enter the **Gulf of Khambhat**. Like other west-flowing rivers, it does not form a delta on the eastern plains. *Hence, option B is incorrect.*
 
• The **Godavari Delta** is located in the state of **Andhra Pradesh** and is a vital region for **agriculture**, particularly **paddy cultivation**, due to its rich **alluvial soil**. *Hence, option C is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Godavari River Features:**

 
 
• It originates from **Trimbakeshwar** in the **Nasik** district of **Maharashtra** at an elevation of about **1,067 meters**.
 
• The total length of the river is approximately **1,465 km**, making it the second-longest river in **India** after the **Ganga**.
 
• Its **drainage basin** extends over the states of **Maharashtra** (about **50%**), **Telangana**, **Andhra Pradesh**, **Chhattisgarh**, and **Odisha**.
 
• Important **tributaries** include the **Purna**, **Wardha**, **Pranhita**, **Manjra**, **Wainganga**, and **Penganga**.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River:**
 
 
• It rises from the **Amarkantak** plateau in **Madhya Pradesh** and flows through a **rift valley** between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges.
 
• It covers a distance of **1,312 km** and forms the famous **Dhuandhar Falls** in **Jabalpur**.
 
 
 
• **Tapi River:**
 
 
• It originates in the **Satpura ranges**, specifically in the **Betul** district of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It flows parallel to the **Narmada** but is much shorter in length, approximately **724 km**.
 
 
 
• **Mahi River:**
 
 
• It is one of the few rivers in **India** that crosses the **Tropic of Cancer** twice.
 
• It flows through **Vadhvana** and drains into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Delta vs. Estuary:** A **delta** is a triangular landform created by deposition of sediment at the mouth of a river, typical of the **Eastern Coast** of **India**. An **estuary** is a partially enclosed coastal body of water where freshwater meets saltwater, typical of the **Western Coast**.
 
• **Eastern Coastal Plain:** This plain is broader and more leveled compared to the **Western Coastal Plain**, providing sufficient space for **sediment deposition** and the formation of large **deltas**.
 
• **Economic Significance:** The **deltaic regions** of the **East Coast** are often referred to as the **"Rice Granary of South India"** due to their high **agricultural productivity** enabled by the **Godavari** and **Krishna** rivers.

questions.question: Three solid cubes whose edges measure 1 cm, 6 cm, and 8 cm, respectively, are melted and recast into a single cube. What is the length (in cm) of the diagonal of the cube?

**∴ Answer = 9√3 cm**

__
 
• **Statement 1: It is a quasi-judicial body** – The **Finance Commission** is indeed a **quasi-judicial body** as it has the authority to recommend the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the States, and among the states themselves, based on principles of equity and justice. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Statement 2: It is related to Article 280** – The Finance Commission is constituted under **Article 280** of the **Indian Constitution**. This article mandates the President to set up a Finance Commission to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the central and state governments. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Statement 3: It is constituted by the President** – The Finance Commission is constituted by the **President of India** every five years or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary. The President appoints its members and defines its terms of reference. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Statement 4: It is constituted after each 6 years** – This statement is incorrect because the Finance Commission is constituted every **five years**, not six years, as per Article 280 of the Constitution. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Composition of the Finance Commission:**

 
 
• The Finance Commission consists of a **Chairman and four other members**. The qualifications of the Chairman and members are prescribed by the Parliament.
 
• The Chairman is typically a person with experience in public affairs, while other members are selected for their expertise in finance, economics, administration, or law.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Finance Commission:**
 
 
• It makes recommendations on the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the **Union and the States**.
 
• It defines the principles that govern grants-in-aid to the states from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
• It also advises on measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.

• The first Finance Commission was established in **1951** under the chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**.
 
• The most recent, **15th Finance Commission**, was chaired by **N.K. Singh**, and its recommendations covered the period from **2021-26**.
 
 
 
• **Reports and Recommendations:**
 
 
• The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and not binding on the government.
 
• However, they hold significant importance in ensuring equitable distribution of resources between the Centre and the States.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 280**: It states that the President shall constitute a Finance Commission at intervals of **five years** or earlier if necessary.
 
• The Finance Commission's recommendations are crucial for maintaining **fiscal federalism** in India.
 
• It plays a vital role in addressing fiscal imbalances between the Centre and the States.
 
• Its recommendations cover revenue-sharing, fiscal consolidation, and grants for various sectors like health, education, and rural development.

__
 
• **Copper** is a chemical element with the symbol **Cu** and atomic **number 29**. It is a soft, malleable, and ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity.
 
• **Option A**, **Rubber**, is a material that resists the flow of electric current because its electrons are tightly bound within its molecular structure. It is classified as an **insulator** and is commonly used to coat electrical wires for safety. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• **Option B**, **Wood**, particularly when dry, does not have free-moving electrons necessary to conduct electricity. It is widely used as a structural material and an **insulator** in various electrical applications. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• **Option C**, **Copper**, is the most common material used for **electrical wiring** in buildings and electronic devices worldwide because it allows electricity to flow with very little **resistance**. *Hence, statement C is correct.*
 
• **Option D**, **Glass**, is a non-crystalline material that prevents the movement of electric charges. Because of its high **resistivity**, it is used as an **insulator** in high-voltage power transmission lines to prevent current from leaking to the ground. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Conductors** are materials that permit the flow of energy. In the context of electricity, conductors allow **electrons** to move freely from atom to atom. Metals like **Silver**, **Copper**, and **Gold** are the best known examples.
 
• **Silver** actually possesses higher electrical conductivity than copper; however, it is not used in general **wiring** due to its high **cost** and tendency to tarnish. **Copper** remains the industry standard for its balance of performance and **affordability**.
 
• **Aluminum** is another significant conductor used primarily in **overhead power transmission lines**. While it has only about **61%** of the conductivity of copper, it is much **lighter** and less expensive, making it ideal for long-distance spans.
 
• The **International Annealed Copper Standard (IACS)** was established in the **year 1913** by the **International Electrotechnical Commission**. It defines the conductivity of commercially pure annealed copper as **100%**, against which all other metallic conductors are measured.
 
• **Insulators** are the opposite of conductors. They have high **resistance** and are used to protect individuals from the **electric shocks** that can occur if a person touches a live wire. Common examples include **Plastic**, **Ceramic**, and **Teflon**.

A low resistivity indicates a material that readily allows electric current. **Copper** has a resistivity of approximately **1.68 x 10^-8 ohm-meters** at **20 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Conductivity**: Several physical factors influence how well a material conducts electricity, including **temperature**, **impurities**, and **electromagnetic fields**. For most metals, as the **temperature** increases, the electrical **resistance** also increases.
 
• **Semiconductors**: These are materials with electrical conductivity between that of a conductor and an insulator. **Silicon** and **Germanium** are the most prominent examples, forming the basis of the modern **electronics industry**, including **transistors**, **diodes**, and **integrated circuits**.
 
• **Applications**: Beyond wiring, **Copper** is essential in the manufacturing of **electric motors**, **generators**, **transformers**, and **renewable energy systems** like **solar panels** and **wind turbines**, where high efficiency is required.

questions.question: Who is responsible for loading the operating system into memory during the booting process?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BIOS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIOS**, which stands for **Basic Input/Output System**, is a critical **firmware** program stored on a small **non-volatile memory** chip (usually **ROM** or **Flash memory**) located on the computer's **motherboard**.
 
• The primary function of the **BIOS** is to serve as an intermediary between the computer **hardware** and the **Operating System**. It is the first piece of software to run when a user presses the power button.
 
• During the startup phase, the **BIOS** performs a diagnostic routine known as **POST (Power-On Self-Test)**. This process checks the integrity of the **CPU**, **RAM**, and hardware controllers like the **keyboard** and **disk drives** to ensure the system is ready to function.
 
• Once the hardware is verified, the **BIOS** searches for a **bootable device**, such as a **Hard Disk Drive (HDD)**, **Solid State Drive (SSD)**, or **USB drive**, based on a pre-configured **Boot Priority** list.
 
• After identifying the device, the **BIOS** locates the **Master Boot Record (MBR)** or **bootloader** and hands over control to it. This process effectively loads the **Operating System** from the **storage disk** into the **Random Access Memory (RAM)** for execution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)**: Historically, the **BIOS** was stored in **ROM** chips because the data remains intact even when the power is turned off. In modern systems, **EEPROM** or **Flash memory** is used so that **BIOS updates** (flashing) can be performed to improve compatibility or security.
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)**: This is the **volatile memory** where the **Operating System** resides while the computer is running. While the **BIOS** is the "agent" that loads the software, the **RAM** is the "destination" where the **OS** is stored for high-speed access by the **CPU**.
 
• **CPU (Central Processing Unit)**: Known as the **processor**, it executes the instructions provided by the **BIOS** during the initial **booting** phase. Without the **BIOS** providing the initial instruction set (the **reset vector**), the **CPU** would not know how to interact with the rest of the hardware upon startup.
 
• **UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface)**: Most modern computers (manufactured after **2010**-**2012**) have replaced the traditional **BIOS** with **UEFI**. **UEFI** supports larger **hard drives** (greater than **2.2 Terabytes**), faster **boot times**, **Secure Boot** features, and a **Graphical User Interface (GUI)** that supports **mouse** input.
 
• **CMOS Battery**: A small **lithium battery** (usually a **CR2032**) on the **motherboard** provides power to the **CMOS chip**, which stores **BIOS settings** such as the **system time**, **date**, and **hardware configurations** when the main power is disconnected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History**: The term **BIOS** was first coined by **Gary Kildall** in **1975** for the **CP/M operating system**. It became a standard in the **IBM PC** launched in **1981**.
 
• **Cold Booting vs. Warm Booting**: **Cold Booting** occurs when the computer is started from a completely powered-off state, involving a full **POST**. **Warm Booting** (Restarting) happens while the power is already on, often skipping some hardware checks to save time.
 
• **Bootloader**: Examples of **bootloaders** that the **BIOS** initiates include **GRUB** (commonly used in **Linux**) and **Windows Boot Manager** (used in **Windows 10** and **Windows 11**).
 
• **Firmware vs. Software**: **BIOS** is considered **firmware** because it is hardware-specific code embedded directly into the machine, whereas the **Operating System** is **software** that runs on top of the **firmware**.

questions.question: Identify an example of a curved mirror.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shining spoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **shining spoon** is the most common household example of a **curved mirror**, specifically a **spherical mirror**. Because its surface is not flat, it reflects light in a way that can magnify or diminish the appearance of an object.
 
• The **inner curved surface** of the spoon acts as a **concave mirror**. When an object is placed very close to it, it forms an **enlarged and erect image**, but as the object moves away, the image becomes **inverted**. ***Hence, option B is correct.***
 
• The **outer bulging surface** of the spoon acts as a **convex mirror**. This side always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image** of the object, regardless of the distance.
 
• A **ladle** is a large, long-handled spoon used for serving liquids. While a polished metal ladle can technically act as a curved mirror, in scientific pedagogy and standard textbooks like **NCERT**, the **shining spoon** is the specific example used to demonstrate **concave and convex** properties. ***Hence, option A is less accurate in a standard testing context.***
 
• A **prism** is a transparent optical element with flat, polished surfaces that **refracts light**. It is primarily used to demonstrate the **dispersion of light** into its constituent colors (VIBGYOR) rather than acting as a mirror. ***Hence, option C is incorrect.***
 
• A **wooden spatula** is an opaque object with a rough surface. Wood does not have a **regular reflection** surface, meaning it cannot form a clear image and thus cannot function as a mirror. ***Hence, option D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirrors (Converging Mirrors)**: These mirrors curve **inward**. They are widely used in **solar furnaces** to focus sunlight, by **dentists** to see large images of teeth, and in **shaving mirrors** to see a magnified view of the face.
 
• **Convex Mirrors (Diverging Mirrors)**: These mirrors curve **outward**. They are used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles because they provide a **wider field of view**, allowing drivers to see much more traffic behind them than a plane mirror would.
 
• **Spherical Mirrors**: These are mirrors whose reflecting surface is a part of a **hollow sphere** of glass. The **center of curvature (C)** is the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part, and the **radius (R)** is the distance from the **pole (P)** to the center.
 
• **Image Nature**: **Real images** are formed when light rays actually meet after reflection and can be caught on a **screen**. **Virtual images** are formed when rays appear to meet and cannot be caught on a screen.
 
• **Reflection Laws**: Every curved mirror follows the **Laws of Reflection**, where the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection** at every point on the surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Focal Length (f)**: For a spherical mirror of small aperture, the **focal length** is exactly half of its **radius of curvature (R)**, expressed by the formula **R = 2f**.
 
• **Mirror Formula**: The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by **1/v + 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Magnification (m)**: This is the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**. For mirrors, it is also expressed as **m = -v/u**. questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends Ajay and Amit, are in the ratio 6 : 7 respectively and each of them saves ₹63,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 2 : 4, find the monthly income of Ajay (in ₹).

Savings units = Income − Expenditure = 6 − 1 = 5 units (for Ajay).

Given 5 units = 63,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 12,600.

Ajay's Income = 6 units × 12,600 = 75,600.

**∴ Answer = 75,600**

questions.question: In October 2025, the broad-daylight heist involving the theft of royal jewellery from the Louvre Museum occurred in which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**France**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Louvre Museum** (Musée du Louvre) is located in **Paris**, **France**. It is the world's most-visited museum and a historic landmark situated on the **Right Bank** of the **Seine River**.
 
• The **royal jewellery** of **France**, known as the **French Crown Jewels** (Joyaux de la Couronne de France), are primarily housed within the **Galerie d'Apollon** (Apollo Gallery) of the **Louvre**. ***Hence, the heist occurred in France.***
 
• The museum was originally built as the **Louvre Castle** in the late **12th** to **13th century** under **Philip II**. Remnants of the medieval fortress are still visible in the museum's basement.
 
• The **Louvre** was established as a public museum during the **French Revolution** in **1793**, showcasing the royal collections to the nation. It has since expanded to house over **38,000 objects** from prehistory to the **21st century**.
 
• The facility covers an area of approximately **72,735 square meters** (**782,910 square feet**), making it the largest art museum in the world by gallery space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The French Crown Jewels:** This collection includes crowns, orb, sceptres, and diamonds that were used by the **French Kings** and **Queens**. One of the most famous items is the **Regent Diamond**, weighing **140.64 carats**, which was acquired by **Philippe II, Duke of Orléans**, in **1717**.
 
• **The Sancy Diamond:** Another notable piece in the collection is the **Sancy Diamond**, a pale yellow diamond of **55.23 carats**, which has a history involving various European monarchs before being secured by the **French** state.
 
• **The Louvre Pyramid:** A modern architectural marvel, the **Louvre Pyramid** was designed by architect **I. M. Pei** and completed in **1989**. It serves as the main entrance to the museum and is composed of **673 glass segments**.
 
• **Famous Artworks:** Apart from jewellery, the **Louvre** is home to the **Mona Lisa** by **Leonardo da Vinci**, the **Venus de Milo**, and the **Winged Victory of Samothrace**. The **Mona Lisa** itself was famously stolen in **1911** by **Vincenzo Peruggia**, which significantly increased the museum's global profile.
 
• **Administrative Control:** The museum is managed by the **French Ministry of Culture** and receives millions of visitors annually, with **7.8 million** recorded in **2022**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Security and Heists:** High-profile museums like the **Louvre** employ advanced **biometric systems**, **laser sensors**, and **24-hour armed security** to protect artifacts. A heist involving royal jewellery would likely target the **Apollo Gallery**, which was renovated in **2020** to enhance the display and safety of the **Crown Jewels**.
 
• **Historical Reorganization:** Many pieces of the **French Crown Jewels** were sold by the **Third Republic** in **1887** to prevent royalist uprisings, but the most historically significant pieces were retained for public display in **France**.
 
• **Global Context:** Similar museums in other countries, such as the **Prado Museum** in **Spain** or the **Uffizi Gallery** in **Italy**, also house significant national treasures, but the specific combination of **royal jewellery** and the **Louvre** identifies the country as **France**.
 
• **International Cooperation:** In the event of a major theft in **2025**, organizations like **INTERPOL** (headquartered in **Lyon**, **France**) would be involved in the international tracking of stolen cultural property through the **Stolen Works of Art Database**.

questions.question: The Poligar Rebellion took place in which part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Poligar Rebellion** (or the Palaiyakkarar Wars) was a significant armed resistance against the **British East India Company** that took place in the southern part of **India**, specifically in the state of **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The rebellion occurred between **1799** and **1805**, originating from the **Tirunelveli**, **Ramanathapuram**, **Sivaganga**, and **Madurai** regions.
 
• The primary cause of the conflict was the **British** attempt to establish direct control over the **Palayams** (administrative territories) and their demand for high land **revenue** or tribute from the local chieftains.
 
• The **First Poligar War** of **1799** was led by the famous chieftain **Veerapandiya Kattabomman** of **Panchalamkurichi**. He defied the **British** authority and refused to pay taxes, leading to a fierce battle. *Since the rebellion was centered in the southern districts of the Madras Presidency, the statement identifying the location as Tamil Nadu is correct.*
 
• The **Second Poligar War** (1800–1801) involved a broader confederacy of local leaders including the **Marudu Pandiyar** brothers, **Gopala Nayak**, and **Oomathurai**, which spread the resistance across much of **South India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Veerapandiya Kattabomman:** He was a 18th-century **Poligar** and chieftain of **Panchalamkurichi** in **Tamil Nadu**. He is celebrated as a folk hero for his refusal to submit to **British** demands. He was eventually captured and executed by hanging at **Kayathar** on **16 October 1799**.
 
• **The Marudu Brothers:** **Periya Marudu** and **Chinna Marudu** were the rulers of **Sivaganga**. They issued the **Tiruchirappalli Proclamation** in **1801**, calling for an all-India unity against the **British**, which was one of the earliest documents advocating for **Indian Independence**.
 
• **The Poligar System:** The **Palaiyakkarar** system was an administrative and military system evolved by the **Nayaks of Madurai** around **1529**. The **Poligars** acted as local **administrative** heads, **judiciary** officers, and military commanders for their respective **Palayams**.
 
• **Carnatic Treaty of 1801:** After the suppression of the **Poligars**, the **British East India Company** forced the **Nawab of Arcot** to sign the **Carnatic Treaty** on **31 July 1801**. This treaty gave the **British** direct **administrative** control over **Tamil Nadu** and effectively ended the **Poligar** system by disarming them.
 
• **Other Regional Rebellions:** For context, the **Sanyasi Rebellion** occurred in **Bengal** (1763-1800), the **Paika Rebellion** took place in **Odisha** (1817), and the **Ramosi Uprising** happened in **Maharashtra** (1822).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"Poligar"** is an English corruption of the **Tamil** word **"Palaiyakkarar"**, which literally means the holder of a **Palayam** (a military camp or a small kingdom).
 
• **Puli Thevar** is often credited as the first **Poligar** to revolt against the **British** in **India** as early as **1757**, nearly a hundred years before the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• The **Poligar Wars** were marked by **guerilla warfare** tactics used by the local chieftains against the superior **artillery** and disciplined ranks of the **British** army.
 
• Following the defeat of the **Poligars**, the **British** demolished several **forts** in **Tamil Nadu** and strictly prohibited the **Poligars** from maintaining private **armies** to prevent future uprisings.

questions.question: Which of the following folk songs is specifically associated with Haryana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ragini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ragini** is the most famous and culturally significant folk song genre of **Haryana**. It is deeply ingrained in the rural lifestyle and is an essential part of the state's oral tradition.
 
• This musical form is closely linked with **Saang** (or **Swang**), a popular folk theatrical form prevalent in **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and **Western Uttar Pradesh**. The songs within a **Saang** performance are generally referred to as **Raginis**.
 
• The legendary folk artist **Pandit Lakhmi Chand**, often honored with titles like **Suryakavi** and the **Shakespeare of Haryana**, is credited with popularizing **Ragini** in the **20th century**. His compositions covered a wide array of themes, from **philosophy** and **spirituality** to **mythology**.
 
• The themes of **Ragini** typically revolve around **heroic deeds**, **historical events**, **religious parables**, and **moral values**. It serves not just as entertainment but also as a medium for **social education** in rural areas.
 
• Instruments such as the **Sarangi**, **Harmonium**, **Dholak**, and **Nagada** are traditionally used to provide the rhythmic and melodic backbone to these performances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhatiali:**

 
 
• This is a traditional folk music form from **Bengal**, specifically **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• It is primarily the music of **boatmen** (known as **Majhis**). The word is derived from **Bhata**, which signifies the downstream flow of a river or the ebb tide.
 
• The songs are characterized by long, melancholic notes that reflect the vastness of the rivers and the solitude of the boatmen.
 
 
 
• **Mand:**
 
 
• **Mand** is a highly sophisticated style of folk singing from **Rajasthan**. It occupies a unique space between **folk** and **Indian Classical Music**.
 
• It originated in the royal courts and is famously associated with the **Marwar** region, including **Jaisalmer** and **Bikaner**.
 
• The world-famous song **"Kesariya Balam"** is composed in the **Mand** style. Celebrated singers like **Allah Jilai Bai** have brought international recognition to this form.
 
 
 
• **Folk Music of Haryana:**
 
 
• Apart from **Ragini**, **Haryana** is home to other folk forms like **Jhumar** (a dance-song for women), **Phag** (sung during the **Holi** festival), and **Panhari**.
 
• The music is often robust and rhythmic, reflecting the martial and agricultural heritage of the **Jat** and **Ahir** communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Identity:** **Haryana** was established as a separate state on **1st November 1966**. Since its inception, the promotion of **Ragini** has been a core part of its cultural identity.
 
• **Modern Evolution:** In the contemporary era, **Ragini** has transitioned from open-air village stages to digital platforms and recorded music, maintaining its popularity among the **Haryanvi diaspora**.
 
• **Linguistic Features:** These songs are typically written and performed in the **Haryanvi dialect** (a variant of **Hindi**), known for its directness and earthy humor.
 
• **Socio-Political Role:** During the **Indian Independence Movement** and various social reform phases, **Raginis** were used to mobilize the masses and spread messages of **patriotism** and **equality**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about functions of the Natural environment?

options.text: The environment sustains life by providing genetics and biodiversity.
Environment does not provide aesthetic services.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environment does not provide aesthetic services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The environment performs four vital functions: supplying **resources**, assimilating **waste**, sustaining **life**, and providing **aesthetic services**.
 
• **Statement A: Environment assimilates waste.** The environment acts as a massive sink that absorbs the by-products of **production** and **consumption**. Natural processes like decomposition by **bacteria** and **fungi** help in recycling organic matter back into the ecosystem. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Statement B: The environment sustains life by providing genetics and biodiversity.** It provides essential life-support systems such as **sunlight**, **water**, and **air**. **Genetic diversity** ensures the resilience of species, while **biodiversity** maintains the balance of ecosystems required for survival. ***Hence, statement B is correct.***
 
• **Statement C: Environment does not provide aesthetic services.** This statement is false because the environment provides significant **aesthetic** and **recreational services**, such as the beauty of **landscapes**, **mountains**, and **oceans**, which improve the quality of human life. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement D: Environment supplies resources.** The environment is the source of all raw materials. It provides **renewable resources** (like **timber** and **water**) that can be replenished and **non-renewable resources** (like **fossil fuels** and **minerals**) that are finite. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• The **incorrect** function listed among the statements is that the environment does not provide aesthetic services, as it is actually one of its primary **cultural services**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Ecosystem Services:** According to the **Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (2005)**, environmental functions are categorized into four types: **Provisioning** (food, water), **Regulating** (climate control), **Cultural** (spiritual, aesthetic), and **Supporting** (nutrient cycling).
 
• **Absorptive Capacity:** This refers to the ability of the environment to absorb **degradation** or **pollution** without causing permanent damage. When **waste generation** exceeds this capacity, it leads to an **environmental crisis**.
 
• **Renewable vs. Non-Renewable:** **Renewable resources** are those that can be used without the possibility of the resource becoming depleted (e.g., **solar energy**). **Non-renewable resources** are those which get exhausted with use (e.g., **coal**, **petroleum**).
 
• **Carrying Capacity:** This is a critical concept in **environmental economics**. It implies that the **resource extraction** should remain below the rate of **resource regeneration**, and waste generated should be within the **assimilative capacity** of the environment.
 
• **Economic Significance:** The environment is not just a biological entity but an **economic asset**. The valuation of **ecosystem services** helps in policy making and **sustainable development** planning globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Crisis:** When the **demand** for resources exceeds the **supply** or the **waste** exceeds the **assimilation capacity**, it results in issues like **global warming**, **ozone depletion**, and **loss of biodiversity**.
 
• **Aesthetic Value Examples:** Scenic beauty is utilized in **Eco-tourism**, which is a major source of revenue for many countries like **India**, **Costa Rica**, and **Kenya**. National Parks like **Jim Corbett** or **Kaziranga** serve both **conservation** and **aesthetic** purposes.
 
• **Sustainable Development:** To maintain the functions of the environment for **future generations**, the concept of **sustainable development** was popularized by the **Brundtland Commission** in its **1987 report**, "Our Common Future."
 
• **Interdependence:** The functions are **interlinked**; for instance, if **waste assimilation** fails due to high pollution, the **life-sustaining** function (biodiversity) is automatically compromised.

questions.question: A boat takes 8 hours to row 72 km downstream and 12 hours to row the same distance upstream. Find the boat's rate in still water and the rate of current, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream Speed (D) = 72 ÷ 8 = 9 km/hr

Upstream Speed (U) = 72 ÷ 12 = 6 km/hr

Boat speed in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (9 + 6) ÷ 2 = 7.5 km/hr

Rate of current = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (9 − 6) ÷ 2 = 1.5 km/hr

**∴ Answer = 7.5 km/hr and 1.5 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Total distance = 72 km

Time taken downstream = 8 hours

Time taken upstream = 12 hours

**Formula used:**

Downstream Speed (D) = Boat Speed (u) + Current Speed (v)

Upstream Speed (U) = Boat Speed (u) − Current Speed (v)

u = (D + U) ÷ 2 and v = (D − U) ÷ 2

 Distance = 72 km 
• Downstream (8h): D = 9 km/h 
 Upstream (12h): U = 6 km/h 
 Boat (u) = (9+6)/2 = 7.5 km/hr Current (v) = (9-6)/2 = 1.5 km/hr 

**Calculations:**

Downstream Speed (D) = 72 ÷ 8 = 9 km/hr

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 72 ÷ 12 = 6 km/hr

⇒ Speed of boat in still water (u) = (9 + 6) ÷ 2

⇒ u = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5 km/hr

⇒ Rate of current (v) = (9 − 6) ÷ 2

⇒ v = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream and Upstream Speed

Downstream speed is the sum of boat speed and stream speed (u + v), while upstream is the difference (u − v).

Speed of Boat and Current

Boat speed (u) = (D + U) ÷ 2 and Stream speed (v) = (D − U) ÷ 2, where D and U are downstream and upstream speeds.

Average Speed of Boat

If a boat travels the same distance downstream and upstream, average speed = (D × U) ÷ u, where u is speed in still water.

questions.question: A boat travels 36 km downstream and 24 km upstream, taking a total of 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, the time taken (in hours) for each journey, respectively, is:

Total time taken for both journeys is 6 hours (Tdₒwₙ + Tᵤₚ = 6).

Speed difference (Downstream − Upstream) must equal 2 × stream speed = 4 km/h.

Check Option 4 (3.0 and 3.0): Downstream Speed = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 km/h.

Upstream Speed = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 km/h.

Difference = 12 − 8 = 4 km/h, which matches the required condition.

**∴ Answer = (3.0 and 3.0)**

**Given:**

Downstream Distance = 36 km, Upstream Distance = 24 km

Total time = 6 hours, Speed of stream (v) = 2 km/h

**Formula used:**

Downstream Speed (D) = u + v, Upstream Speed (U) = u − v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
• 
 Stream (v = 2 km/h) BOAT 
• 
 Downstream: 36 km 
• 
 Upstream: 24 km Total Journey Time = 6 hrs 

**Calculations:**

Let speed of boat in still water be u km/h.

⇒ 36 ÷ (u + 2) + 24 ÷ (u − 2) = 6

⇒ 6 ÷ (u + 2) + 4 ÷ (u − 2) = 1

⇒ 6(u − 2) + 4(u + 2) = (u + 2)(u − 2)

⇒ 6u − 12 + 4u + 8 = u² − 4

⇒ 10u − 4 = u² − 4 ⇒ u² − 10u = 0

⇒ u = 10 km/h (Since u cannot be 0)

⇒ Time Downstream = 36 ÷ (10 + 2) = 3.0 hours

⇒ Time Upstream = 24 ÷ (10 − 2) = 3.0 hours

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

Still Water Speed (u)

The speed of the boat when the water is stationary. u = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Stream Speed (v)

The rate at which the river water flows. v = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Downstream and Upstream

Downstream is with the flow (u+v), while Upstream is against the flow (u−v).

Average Speed for Round Trip

For equal distances, Average Speed = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still Water Speed.

questions.question: Evaluate: 16 + 20 ÷ 4 - 3 × 3

Perform Division and Multiplication first according to BODMAS: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 3 × 3 = 9.

Rewrite the simplified expression: 16 + 5 − 9.

**Given:**

Expression: 16 + 20 ÷ 4 − 3 × 3

**Formula used:**

BODMAS Rule: Solve operations in the order of Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

 BODMAS Calculation Steps 
• Original: 16 + 20 ÷ 4 − 3 × 3 Simplified: 16 + 5 − 9 → 12 Left to right: Div/Mult then Add/Sub 

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Division (20 ÷ 4)

⇒ 16 + 5 − 3 × 3

Step 2: Multiplication (3 × 3)

⇒ 16 + 5 − 9

Step 3: Addition (16 + 5)

⇒ 21 − 9

Step 4: Subtraction (21 − 9)

⇒ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12 (Option 4).**

VBODMAS Rule

V stands for Vinculum (a bar bracket like 5 − 2 over numbers), which takes the highest precedence before brackets.

Priority Levels

Division and Multiplication are of the same rank; Addition and Subtraction are of the same rank. Solve them as they appear from left to right.

The 'Of' Operation

'Of' represents multiplication but must be solved before regular Division and Multiplication (e.g., 20 ÷ 2 of 5 = 20 ÷ 10 = 2).

questions.question: What is the primary role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Break down organic matter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decomposers** are organisms, primarily **microbes** like **bacteria** and **fungi**, that perform the vital function of breaking down **complex organic matter** into simpler **inorganic substances** like carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• The process of capturing **sunlight** to produce energy is known as **photosynthesis**, which is the primary role of **producers** (autotrophs) such as **green plants** and **algae**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• The **production of oxygen** is a biological byproduct of **photosynthesis** carried out by **producers** in the presence of **chlorophyll** and **solar energy**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• **Primary consumers** are **herbivores** that obtain their energy by feeding directly on **producers**; decomposers, instead, occupy the final stage of the **food chain** and act on all **trophic levels** once the organisms die. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***
 
• Decomposers are often referred to as **saprotrophs** because they feed on **dead and decaying** plant and animal remains, ensuring that the **earth** does not become covered in **organic waste**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nutrient Cycling:** Decomposers are essential for **biogeochemical cycles**. They release **Nitrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Potassium** back into the **soil**, making these minerals available again for **producers** to use.
 
• **Detritivores:** These are a specific type of decomposer, such as **earthworms**, **millipedes**, and **woodlice**, that physically ingest **detritus** (dead organic matter) to break it into smaller fragments.
 
• **Saprotrophic Nutrition:** Fungi and certain bacteria exhibit this by secreting **digestive enzymes** directly onto the **dead matter**. The enzymes break down the matter **extracellularly**, and the resulting nutrients are then absorbed by the organism.
 
• **Environmental Factors:** The rate of **decomposition** is heavily influenced by **temperature**, **moisture**, and **oxygen availability**. Warm and moist environments, like **tropical rainforests**, see rapid decomposition, whereas cold **tundra** regions have very slow rates.
 
• **Waste Management:** Naturally occurring decomposers are utilized in **sewage treatment plants** and **biogas plants** to convert **human waste** and **agricultural residue** into **methane** and **compost**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fragmentation:** This is the initial step of **decomposition** where **detritivores** break down **detritus** into smaller particles to increase the **surface area** for microbial action.
 
• **Leaching:** This process involves **water-soluble inorganic nutrients** moving down into the **soil profile** and becoming precipitated as unavailable **salts**.
 
• **Humification:** It leads to the accumulation of **humus**, a dark-colored **amorphous substance** that is highly resistant to **microbial action** and acts as a **nutrient reservoir** for the soil.
 
• **Mineralization:** This is the final step where the **humus** is further degraded by some microbes, resulting in the release of **inorganic nutrients** back into the ecosystem.
 
• **Energy Flow:** Unlike **nutrients**, which **cycle** through the ecosystem, **energy** flows **unidirectionally** from the sun and is eventually lost as **heat**, meaning decomposers do not "create" energy but rather **recycle** chemical components.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the keyboard shortcut Alt + F4 in Windows?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To close the active window**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alt + F4** is a standard keyboard shortcut in the **Microsoft Windows** operating system designed to **close the currently active window** or application immediately.
 
• To minimize the active window, users typically use the **Windows Logo Key + Down Arrow** or **Alt + Space + N**. ***Hence, Option A is incorrect.***
 
• Opening **File Explorer** is achieved through the **Windows Logo Key + E** shortcut, which provides quick access to files and folders. ***Hence, Option B is incorrect.***
 
• The primary function of the **Alt + F4** combination is to signal the **active window** to terminate its process and close. ***Hence, Option C is correct.***
 
• Switching between open applications is performed using the **Alt + Tab** shortcut, which opens a thumbnail view of all running programs for rapid navigation. ***Hence, Option D is incorrect.***
 
• If no windows are active (i.e., the user is on the **Desktop**), pressing **Alt + F4** will trigger the **Shut Down Windows** dialog box, offering options to **Restart**, **Sleep**, or **Shut Down** the **PC**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** The **Alt + F4** shortcut is part of the **Common User Access (CUA)** standard, which was first published in **1987** by **IBM**. This standard aimed to create a uniform set of **keyboard shortcuts** across different software applications and **operating systems**.
 
• **Operating System Compatibility:** While primarily associated with **Windows** (from early versions like **Windows 3.1** to modern **Windows 11**), similar concepts exist in other environments, though **macOS** uses **Command + Q** to quit applications.
 
• **Productivity Features:** **Keyboard shortcuts** are essential **functions** that reduce reliance on the computer mouse, thereby increasing **efficiency** and **productivity** for professionals, developers, and regular users.
 
• **System Troubleshooting:** **Alt + F4** is often used as a quick **troubleshooting** step to **force-close** applications that have become unresponsive or are "hanging," preventing them from consuming further **CPU** or **RAM** resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference from Ctrl + F4:** It is important to distinguish between **Alt + F4** and **Ctrl + F4**. While **Alt + F4** closes the entire application, **Ctrl + F4** is used to close only the **active document** or **tab** within an application (like a single spreadsheet in **Excel** or a tab in **web browsers**).
 
• **Data Safety:** When using **Alt + F4**, most modern **software** applications will provide a **dialog box** asking the user to **save changes** before the window closes, preventing accidental **data loss**.
 
• **Application in Gaming:** In many full-screen **PC games**, **Alt + F4** acts as an "emergency exit" to immediately quit to the **desktop**, although some modern games may disable this feature to prevent accidental exits.
 
• **Accessibility:** For users with **motor impairments**, memorizing **keyboard shortcuts** like **Alt + F4** provides an alternative way to manage the **user interface** without requiring the fine motor control needed for a mouse.

questions.question: In which district of Gujarat is the Harappan archaeological site of Dholavira, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kutch District**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira** is an ancient **Harappan** city located on the **Khadir Bet** island in the **Kutch Desert Wildlife Sanctuary** in the **Great Rann of Kutch**, **Gujarat**.
 
• It was discovered by archaeologist **Jagat Pati Joshi** (J.P. Joshi) in **1967-68** and is the **fifth-largest** of the eight major Harappan sites, dating back to approximately **2650 BCE**.
 
• In **July 2021**, **Dholavira** was inscribed as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**, becoming the **40th** site in **India** and the first site of the **Indus Valley Civilization** in **India** to receive this prestigious tag.
 
• One of the most remarkable **features** of **Dholavira** is its sophisticated **water management system**, which included a series of **reservoirs**, step-wells, and channels to harvest and store rainwater in an arid environment.
 
• Unlike other **Indus Valley Civilization** cities that were typically divided into two parts, **Dholavira** was unique for its **tripartite layout**, consisting of a **Citadel**, a **Middle Town**, and a **Lower Town**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lothal:** Located in the **Ahmedabad District** of **Gujarat**, it is famous for having the world’s earliest known **artificial dockyard**, which connected the city to an ancient course of the **Sabarmati River** for trade.
 
• **Surkotada:** Situated in the **Kutch District**, this site is significant for providing the first actual **remains of horse bones** in the **Indus Valley Civilization**, dating around **2100 BCE**.
 
• **Rakhigarhi:** Located in **Hisar**, **Haryana**, it is currently considered the **largest Harappan site** in the Indian subcontinent, surpassing **Mohenjo-daro** in terms of geographical area.
 
• **Patan District:** While not the primary location for **Dholavira**, **Patan** is home to another **UNESCO World Heritage Site** called **Rani ki Vav** (The Queen’s Stepwell), built in the **11th century** by the **Chaulukya dynasty**.
 
• **Banaskantha District:** This district is located in northern **Gujarat** and is known for the **Ambaji Temple** and its proximity to the **Aravalli Range**, rather than major Harappan urban centers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Signboard:** Archaeologists discovered a unique **"signboard"** in the **Citadel** area of **Dholavira**, containing **10 large-sized symbols** of the **Indus script**, which remains one of the longest inscriptions ever found from the civilization.
 
• **Construction Materials:** While most Harappan cities used **sun-dried** or **burnt mud bricks**, **Dholavira** extensively used **locally quarried stone** for the construction of its massive **fortifications** and structures.
 
• **Trade and Economy:** The city was a major **commercial hub**, engaging in trade with **Mesopotamia** and other regions, specializing in the production of **beads**, **shell jewelry**, and **copper** artifacts.
 
• **Burial Practices:** Excavations at **Dholavira** revealed **megalithic** burial structures, which were circular or rectangular stone enclosures, showing unique **mortuary practices** different from the typical Harappan cemetery burials.

questions.question: How does higher soil moisture retention in black soils influence cropping intensity in regions like Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh?

options.text: It supports multiple cropping cycles by sustaining moisture across seasons
It limits cropping to a single season to prevent waterlogging
It encourages plantation crops over food grains due to deep root support
It reduces the need for crop rotation due to stable nutrient levels

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It supports multiple cropping cycles by sustaining moisture across seasons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Black soil**, also known as **Regur soil**, is characterized by its exceptionally high **clay content**, which gives it a unique ability to **retain moisture** for long durations. This physical property is crucial for agriculture in states like **Maharashtra** and **Madhya Pradesh** where rainfall is seasonal. *Hence, the statement regarding its moisture-sustaining capability is correct.*
 
• The high **water-holding capacity** of this soil allows it to store rainwater during the **Monsoon (Kharif) season** and release it slowly. This enables farmers to grow a second crop during the **Rabi season** (winter) even in areas with limited **irrigation**. *Hence, the claim that it supports multiple cropping cycles is correct.*
 
• In the **Deccan Trap** region, the soil's ability to remain moist facilitates the cultivation of crops like **Wheat**, **Gram**, and **Linseed** after the harvest of primary crops like **Cotton**. This significantly increases the **cropping intensity** of the region, which is the ratio of Net Sown Area to Total Cropped Area. *Hence, the influence on cropping intensity is correctly explained.*
 
• During the dry season, these soils develop **deep cracks**, which assist in **soil aeration** and the nitrogen fixation process. When it rains, the soil swells and becomes **sticky**, sealing the moisture deep within the sub-layers. *Hence, the structural behavior of the soil directly aids in moisture preservation.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation and Composition:**

 
 
• **Black soil** is formed from the weathering of **Basaltic rocks** (igneous rocks) formed by **volcanic eruptions** millions of years ago.
 
• It is rich in soil nutrients such as **Calcium Carbonate**, **Magnesium**, **Potash**, and **Lime**, making it naturally fertile.
 
• However, it is generally **poor in Phosphoric content**, **Nitrogen**, and **Organic matter** (humus).
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distribution:**
 
 
• It covers approximately **15% to 16%** of the total geographical area of **India**, spanning about **5.46 lakh sq km**.
 
• The major distribution is found in the **Deccan Lava Plateau**, covering **Maharashtra**, **Gujarat**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and parts of **Karnataka**, **Andhra Pradesh**, and **Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
 
• **Major Crops:**
 
 
• It is most famous for **Cotton** cultivation, earning the name **Black Cotton Soil**.
 
• Other significant crops grown include **Sugarcane**, **Tobacco**, **Oilseeds** (like **Sunflower** and **Soybean**), and **Citrus fruits**.
 
• In **Madhya Pradesh**, it is the primary soil for massive **Soybean** production, making the state a leader in this sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Self-Plowing Characteristic:** Because the soil develops **wide cracks** during the **summer**, it allows for the oxygenation of the deeper layers. This phenomenon is often referred to as **"self-plowing"** by geologists and agronomists.
 
• **Coloration:** The dark color of the soil is attributed to the presence of small amounts of **Titaniferous Magnetite** or **Iron** and **Aluminum silicates**.
 
• **Tillage Challenges:** Due to its **sticky nature** when wet, the soil is difficult to manage or **tilled** immediately after the first rain. Farmers must plow the land precisely at the right time to ensure proper seedbed preparation.
 
• **Scientific Classification:** In the **USDA soil taxonomy**, black soils are classified under the order **Vertisols**, reflecting their high **expandable clay** content.

400 ÷ 9 = 44 4/9 %.

**∴ Answer = 44 4/9 %**

Time (T) = 9 years

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount − Principal

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

 P=100 A=500 
 SI = 400 
• Time = 9 Years Find Rate % per annum 

**Calculations:**

SI = 500 − 100 = 400

⇒ R = (400 × 100) ÷ (100 × 9) ⇒ R = 400 ÷ 9 ⇒ R = 44 4/9 %

questions.question: Eight years ago from now, the average age of A and B was 24 years. The average age of A, B and C today is 32 years. How old will C be after 16 years from now?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Today, average age of A and B = 24 + 8 = 32 years.

Current average age of A, B and C = 32 years.

Since the average remains same (32) after C joins, C's current age must be 32 years.

Age of C after 16 years = 32 + 16 = 48 years.

**∴ Answer = 48 years**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Average age of A and B (8 years ago) = 24 years

Average age of A, B and C (Today) = 32 years

**Formula used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of Persons

 
• 
 8 Years Ago Sum (A+B) = 48 Today Sum (ABC) = 96 Future (+16y) C = 48 
 +8 years each 
 C + 16 

**Calculations:**

Sum of ages of A and B (8 years ago) = 24 × 2 = 48 years

⇒ Sum of ages of A and B (Today) = 48 + (8 × 2) = 64 years

⇒ Sum of ages of A, B and C (Today) = 32 × 3 = 96 years

⇒ Current age of C = Sum(ABC) − Sum(AB) = 96 − 64 = 32 years

⇒ Age of C after 16 years from now = 32 + 16 = 48 years

**∴ The correct answer is 48 years. (Option 4).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Age Change

If the current average age of n people is X, then after k years, the average age of the same group will be X + k.

Inclusion of New Member

Age of new member = (New Average × New Number of Members) − (Old Average × Old Number of Members).

Deviation Method

If a new person joins and the average remains unchanged, the new person's value is exactly equal to the existing average.

Total Sum Formula

Total Age Sum = Average Age × Total Number of Persons.

questions.question: According to the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Finance Commission shall consist of:

options.text: A Chairman and eight other members
A Chairman and six other members
A Chairman and four other members
A Chairman and two other members

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Finance Commission** is a **Constitutional Body** established by the **President of India** under **Article 280** of the **Constitution**.
 
• As per the **Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951**, the Commission shall consist of a **Chairman** and **four other members**.
 
• The **Chairman** of the Commission is selected from among persons who have had experience in **public affairs**.
 
• The **four other members** are selected from among persons who:
 
 
• Are, or have been, or are qualified to be appointed as **Judges of a High Court**; or
 
• Have special knowledge of the **finances and accounts** of the Government; or
 
• Have had wide experience in **financial matters** and in **administration**; or
 
• Have special knowledge of **economics**.
 
 
 
• Every member of the Commission holds office for such period as may be specified in the order of the **President** and is eligible for **re-appointment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Finance Commission:** It was established in **1951** under the chairmanship of **Shri K.C. Neogy**.
 
• **Fifteenth Finance Commission:** This Commission was constituted in **November 2017**, chaired by **Shri N.K. Singh**. Its recommendations cover a period of **five years** from the year **2021-22** to **2025-26**.
 
• **Sixteenth Finance Commission:** The Government of India, in **December 2023**, constituted the 16th Finance Commission with **Dr. Arvind Panagariya** as the **Chairman**. This commission is expected to submit its report by **October 31, 2025**.
 
• **Constitutional Status:** **Article 280(1)** mandates that the **President** shall, within **two years** from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of every **fifth year**, constitute a Finance Commission.
 
• **Advisory Nature:** It is important to note that the recommendations made by the Finance Commission are only of an **advisory nature** and hence, not binding on the **Government of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distribution of Taxes:** The primary function of the Finance Commission is to recommend the **distribution** between the **Union** and the **States** of the net proceeds of **taxes** which are to be divided between them.
 
• **Grants-in-aid:** It also determines the principles which should govern the **grants-in-aid** of the revenues of the States out of the **Consolidated Fund of India**.
 
• **Panchayats and Municipalities:** The Commission suggests measures needed to augment the **Consolidated Fund of a State** to supplement the resources of the **Panchayats** and **Municipalities** in the State on the basis of the recommendations made by the **Finance Commission of the State**.
 
• **Reports:** Under **Article 281**, the **President** shall cause every recommendation made by the Finance Commission to be laid before each **House of Parliament**.
