questions.question: Which coastal region of India is associated with the Vembanad Lagoon being separated from the Arabian Sea by narrow barrier islands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malabar Coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Malabar Coast** is a long, narrow coastline on the southwestern shore of the **Indian** mainland, stretching from the southern part of **Goa** down to **Kanyakumari** in **Tamil Nadu**. It is primarily situated within the state of **Kerala**.
 
• The **Vembanad Lagoon**, also known as **Vembanad Kayal** or **Vembanad Lake**, is the largest lake in **Kerala** and the **longest lake in India**, stretching over a length of **96.5 km**.
 
• This lagoon is physically separated from the **Arabian Sea** by a series of narrow barrier islands and sandspits. A prominent example is the artificial **Willingdon Island**, which was created in **1936** and is located within the **Kochi** lake area.
 
• The coast is distinguished by its unique **backwaters** (locally called **Kayals**), which are a network of brackish lagoons and lakes lying parallel to the **Arabian Sea**. These are formed by the action of shore currents and waves creating barrier islands.
 
• The **Malabar Coast** is categorized as an **emergent coastline** in some parts and a **submergent coastline** in others, leading to the formation of natural harbors like **Kochi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Coromandel Coast**:

 
 
• It is the southeastern coastal region of **India**, bounded by the **Utkal Plains** to the north and the **Kaveri Delta** to the south.
 
• Unlike the **Malabar Coast**, it remains mostly dry during the **South-West Monsoon** and receives heavy rainfall during the **North-East (Retreating) Monsoon** in **October** and **November**.
 
 
 
• **Konkan Coast**:
 
 
• This coastline extends from **Daman** in the north to **Goa** in the south, covering the states of **Maharashtra** and **Goa**.
 
• It is characterized by rugged terrain, rocky cliffs, and numerous small estuaries, serving as a primary region for the **Konkan Railway**.
 
 
 
• **Northern Circar**:
 
 
• It refers to the northern part of **India's** eastern coast, lying between the **Mahanadi** and **Krishna** rivers.
 
• This region covers parts of **Odisha** and **Andhra Pradesh** and is known for its wide fertile deltas and the **Chilika Lake**, which is **India's largest saltwater lagoon**.
 
 
 
• **Ramsar Convention**:
 
 
• The **Vembanad-Kol** wetland system was recognized as a **Ramsar site** in **2002** due to its international ecological importance.
 
• It is the second-largest **Ramsar site** in **India** after the **Sundarbans** in **West Bengal**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rivers and Feeders**: The **Vembanad Lagoon** is fed by **10** major rivers, including the **Periyar**, **Pamba**, **Meenachil**, **Achankovil**, **Manimala**, and **Muvattupuzha**.
 
• **Economic and Cultural Significance**:
 
 
• It is the venue for the world-famous **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** (Vallam Kali), held annually in the **Punnamada** part of the lake near **Alappuzha**.
 
• The **Thanneermukkom Bund** was constructed in **1974** to prevent saltwater intrusion into the **Kuttanad** region, which is known as the "Rice Bowl of Kerala" and is one of the few places in the world where farming is done **below sea level**.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Kerala**: The state of **Kerala** is often referred to as "God's Own Country," largely due to the scenic beauty of the **Malabar** backwaters and the **Western Ghats**.

questions.question: In what way does the Union Cabinet differ from other government committees?

options.text: It is elected by the public
It functions independently of the Prime Minister
It serves as the supreme decision-making body of the executive branch
It includes members of the judiciary

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It serves as the supreme decision-making body of the executive branch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet** is a smaller body within the **Council of Ministers** consisting of **15 to 20** of the most important senior ministers who hold pivotal portfolios like **Home, Defence, Finance, and External Affairs**.
 
• **Statement A**: It is elected by the public. This is incorrect because, while ministers must be members of the **Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha)** who are elected or nominated, they are specifically appointed to the **Cabinet** by the **President of India** on the advice of the **Prime Minister**. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement B**: It functions independently of the Prime Minister. This is incorrect because the **Prime Minister** is the head of the **Cabinet**, chairs its meetings, and directs its proceedings. The **Prime Minister** has the power to appoint or dismiss ministers. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• **Statement C**: It serves as the supreme decision-making body of the executive branch. This is correct as the **Cabinet** is the real steering wheel of the **Government of India**, responsible for formulating all major policies and taking final decisions on national and international issues. *Hence, statement C is correct.*
 
• **Statement D**: It includes members of the judiciary. This is incorrect because the **Cabinet** is strictly a part of the **Executive branch** of the government. Under the **Separation of Powers**, members of the **Judiciary** (Judges) cannot be part of the **Executive**. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Status:** Originally, the **Constitution of India** (**1950**) did not mention the word **"Cabinet"** in detail; it only spoke of the **Council of Ministers**. The word **"Cabinet"** was inserted into **Article 352** by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**.
 
• **Functions of the Cabinet:** The **Cabinet** acts as the **highest decision-making authority** in the **Indian politico-administrative system**. It is the **chief policy-making body**, the **supreme directing authority** of the Central government, and it deals with all **major legislative and financial matters**.
 
• **Collective Responsibility:** Under **Article 75(3)**, the **Council of Ministers** (including the Cabinet) is **collectively responsible** to the **Lok Sabha**. This means they stand or fall together; a **no-confidence motion** against one minister can lead to the resignation of the entire government.
 
• **Composition:** While the **Council of Ministers** is a large body (usually **60 to 70** ministers), the **Cabinet** is a compact group of **Senior Ministers** who meet frequently (usually once a week) to deliberate on **national security, economic policy, and foreign relations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prime Minister's Role:** The **Prime Minister** acts as the **"Primus Inter Pares"** (First among equals) in the **Cabinet**. He coordinates the work of different departments and has the final say in **Cabinet** deliberations.
 
• **Cabinet Committees:** To reduce the workload, various **Cabinet Committees** are formed, such as the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet**, the **Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)**, and the **Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)**. These committees are mostly headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Article 74:** Mandates that there shall be a **Council of Ministers** with the **Prime Minister** at the head to aid and advise the **President**, who shall act in accordance with such advice.
 
• **Eligibility:** A **Cabinet Minister** must be a member of either house of **Parliament**. If a non-member is appointed, they must be elected to either the **Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha** within a period of **6 months** from the date of appointment.

questions.question: Which central government scheme is primarily aimed at providing road connectivity to rural and remote areas in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)** was launched on **25th December 2000** by the then Prime Minister of India, **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**, to provide **unrestricted all-weather road connectivity** to unconnected habitations.
 
• It is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** falling under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Rural Development**. The primary objective is to connect habitations with a population of **500 and above** in plain areas.
 
• In **hill states**, **tribal areas**, and **desert areas**, the population threshold for eligibility is relaxed to **250 and above** to ensure that remote locations are integrated into the mainstream economy.
 
• The scheme emphasizes the quality of construction and ensures that the roads built are **all-weather roads**, meaning they are trafficable throughout the year, including during the rainy season.
 
• The **funding pattern** for the scheme was originally 100% Central assistance, but since **2015-16**, the cost is shared between the **Union Government** and the **States** in the ratio of **60:40** for most states and **90:10** for the **8 North Eastern** and **3 Himalayan states** (**Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF):** This fund was created by the **Government of India** in **1995-96** and is maintained by **NABARD**. It provides low-cost fund support to **State Governments** and **State-owned corporations** for quick completion of ongoing projects related to **medium and minor irrigation**, **soil conservation**, and other forms of rural infrastructure.
 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana:** This is an ambitious umbrella program for the **highways sector** launched in **2017**. It focuses on optimizing the efficiency of **freight and passenger movement** across the **country** by bridging critical infrastructure gaps through **Economic Corridors**, **Inter-corridors**, and **National Corridors**.
 
• **Setu Bharatam Scheme:** Launched in **March 2016** by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, this scheme aims to make all **National Highways** free of **railway level crossings** by **2019** through the construction of **Rail Over Bridges (ROBs)** and **Rail Under Bridges (RUBs)**.
 
• **PMGSY-II and PMGSY-III:** **PMGSY-II** was approved in **May 2013** to consolidate the existing rural road network, while **PMGSY-III** was launched in **2019** to focus on consolidating through routes and major rural links that connect habitations to **Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs)**, **Higher Secondary Schools**, and **Hospitals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The implementation of PMGSY is monitored through the **Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS)**, which identifies the progress of road works in every **district** and **state** of **India**.
 
• The **National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA)** provides technical and operational support to the **Ministry of Rural Development** for the effective implementation of the program.
 
• The **M Meri Sadak** mobile application was launched in **2015** to enable **citizens** to register complaints regarding the quality and pace of work of PMGSY roads, promoting **transparency** and **accountability**.
 
• Maintenance of the roads built under PMGSY is the responsibility of the **State Governments**, and a **five-year maintenance contract** is typically integrated into the initial construction contract to ensure durability.

questions.question: According to Joule’s law of heating, the heat produced in a resistor is _____________________.

options.text: directly proportional to the square of current
directly proportional to the square of resistance
inversely proportional to the square of current
inversely proportional to the square of resistance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**directly proportional to the square of current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joule’s Law of Heating** states that the heat produced in a resistor is **directly proportional to the square of the current** for a given resistance and time. This means if the current is doubled, the heat produced becomes four times greater. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• According to the law, the heat produced is **directly proportional to the resistance (R)** of the conductor for a given current and time. It is not proportional to the square of the resistance. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• The law establishes a direct relationship between heat and the square of the current, not an inverse one. An inverse relationship would imply heat decreases as current increases, which is physically false in this context. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• Heat is **directly proportional** to the resistance of the wire, meaning a higher resistance produces more heat for the same current. It does not have an inverse relationship with the square of resistance. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***
 
• The mathematical formula for **Joule’s Law** is **H = I²Rt**, where **H** is the heat produced, **I** is the electric current, **R** is the electrical resistance, and **t** is the **time** duration for which the current flows.
 
• This fundamental principle was discovered by the English physicist **James Prescott Joule** in the **year 1841**, which explains how **electrical energy** is converted into **heat energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Power:** The rate at which electrical energy is consumed or dissipated in an electric circuit is known as power. It is given by the formula **P = VI** or **P = I²R**. The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**.
 
• **Applications of Joule Heating:** This principle is utilized in various household appliances such as **electric irons**, **electric toasters**, **electric ovens**, and **room heaters**. These devices use materials with high **resistivity**, like **Nichrome** (an alloy of nickel and chromium), to generate maximum heat.
 
• **Electric Bulb:** In a traditional **incandescent bulb**, the filament is made of **Tungsten** because of its very high **melting point** of approximately **3380°C**. Most of the power consumed by the filament is dissipated as heat, but a small fraction is emitted as light.
 
• **Electric Fuse:** It is a safety device based on the **heating effect of current**. It protects circuits and appliances by stopping the flow of any unduly high electric current. A fuse consists of a piece of wire made of an alloy (like **tin and lead**) with an appropriate **low melting point**. If a current larger than the specified **numerical value** flows, the temperature of the fuse wire increases, causing it to melt and break the circuit.
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** The **resistance** of a conductor depends on its **length**, its **area of cross-section**, and the **nature of its material** (resistivity). According to **Ohm's Law**, **V = IR**, which is closely related to the energy calculations in Joule's law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Units of Measurement:** The **SI unit** of heat produced is the **Joule (J)**, while the practical unit used in older texts or specific contexts is the **Calorie** (1 Calorie is approximately **4.184 Joules**).
 
• **Energy Conservation:** Joule heating is an example of the **Law of Conservation of Energy**, where **potential energy** of electrons is converted into **kinetic energy** and then into **thermal energy** due to collisions within the atomic lattice of the resistor.
 
• **Current and Heat:** Since heat is proportional to the **square of the current**, even a small increase in the **current** can lead to a significant increase in the heat generated, which is why **short circuits** (where resistance is near zero and current becomes very high) often lead to fires.

questions.question: What is one way to monitor the real-time flow of activities on a Windows computer?

options.text: By analyzing processes through File Explorer
By viewing notifications in the Action Center
By checking system performance in the Settings app

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By using Task Manager**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Task Manager** is a system monitor program used to provide information about the processes and applications running on a **Windows** computer, as well as the general status of the computer. It allows users to monitor the real-time flow of activities efficiently.
 
• It provides critical data regarding **CPU** (Central Processing Unit) usage, **Memory** (RAM) consumption, **Disk** activity, and **Network** performance. This real-time tracking helps in identifying resource-heavy applications that might be slowing down the system.
 
• The **Processes** tab displays a list of all active applications and background processes. Each process is assigned a unique **Process ID (PID)**, which is a **numerical value** used by the operating system to identify active programs. *Hence, option C is the correct way to monitor real-time activities.*
 
• Users can utilize **Task Manager** to force-quit unresponsive programs. By selecting a task and clicking **"End Task,"** the system terminates the process immediately, which is a core function for system troubleshooting.
 
• The **Performance** tab in **Task Manager** offers graphical representations of hardware utilization over a specific **time** period, allowing users to see spikes in activity as they happen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **File Explorer:** Formerly known as **Windows Explorer**, this is a file manager application that was first introduced with **Windows 95** in the **year 1995**. Its primary **functions** include navigating the file system, opening folders, and managing files (copy, paste, delete). While it shows files, it does not provide a real-time monitor of system activity or process execution. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• **Action Center:** This feature was introduced in **Windows 7** and expanded in **Windows 10**. It serves as a central **location** for system notifications and quick settings (like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Brightness). While it alerts users to system updates or security issues, it does not track the real-time flow of hardware or software processes. *Hence, statement B is incorrect.*
 
• **Settings App:** Introduced in **Windows 8** and further refined in **Windows 11**, this app is designed to replace the **Control Panel** for general system configuration. While it contains a "Power & Battery" or "Storage" section, it is used for high-level adjustments rather than the granular, second-by-second monitoring provided by specialized tools. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*
 
• **Task Manager History:** The modern version of **Task Manager** was significantly overhauled in **2012** with the release of **Windows 8**, adding the **App History** tab, which tracks resource usage for **Microsoft Store** apps over a **30-day** period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Access Methods:** There are several **features** to access **Task Manager** quickly. The most common keyboard shortcut is **Ctrl + Shift + Esc**, which opens it directly. Alternatively, **Ctrl + Alt + Delete** can be used to access a security screen that includes a link to it.
 
• **Startup Management:** One of the vital **applications** of **Task Manager** is the **Startup** tab. It lists all programs that are configured to run automatically when the computer boots up. Disabling unnecessary startup items can significantly reduce the boot **time** of a **Windows** machine.
 
• **Resource Monitor:** Within the **Performance** tab, there is a link to the **Resource Monitor**. This is an advanced tool that provides even more detailed **data** and **facts** about hardware usage, including individual **Disk** read/write speeds and detailed **TCP** connections for **Network** analysis.
 
• **Services Tab:** **Task Manager** also includes a **Services** tab, which shows the status of system services (either **Running** or **Stopped**). Users can start or stop services here, which is often required during software installations or system debugging.

questions.question: P sells an item to Q at 53% profit. Q sells the same item to R at 68% loss. If R paid ₹ 3060 for the item, then at what price (in ₹) is the item purchased by P?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for 53% profit = 1.53

Multiplying factor for 68% loss = 1 − 0.68 = 0.32

Net multiplying factor = 1.53 × 0.32 = 0.4896

Purchase Price = 3060 ÷ 0.4896 = 6250

**∴ Answer = 6250**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Profit percentage of P = 53%

Loss percentage of Q = 68%

Amount paid by R = ₹ 3060

**Formula used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (100 + Profit %)/100 × (100 − Loss %)/100

 P (CP) 
• 
 +53% Q (CP) 
• 
 −68% R (CP) ₹ 3060 Successive Transfer: P → Q → R 

**Calculations:**

Let the purchase price for P be ₹ x.

⇒ Q's cost price = x × (1 + 53/100) = 1.53x

⇒ R's cost price = 1.53x × (1 − 68/100)

⇒ 3060 = 1.53x × 0.32

⇒ 3060 = 0.4896x

⇒ x = 3060 ÷ 0.4896

⇒ x = 6250

**∴ The correct answer is 6250 (Option 1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

Effective Profit and Loss

The final multiplier for a series of profits (pᵢ) and losses (lᵢ) is (1 + p₁/100) × (1 − l₁/100) × ...

Cost Price and Selling Price Relationship

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss %)/100. In a chain of sales, the SP for the seller is the CP for the buyer.

questions.question: Which of the following temples is an example of Dravidian architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meenakshi Temple, Madurai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Meenakshi Amman Temple**, located in the ancient city of **Madurai**, **Tamil Nadu**, is one of the most prominent examples of **Dravidian architecture**. It is dedicated to **Goddess Meenakshi** (a form of Parvati) and **Lord Sundareswarar** (a form of Shiva). The temple is famous for its **14 gopurams** (gateway towers), with the tallest reaching over **170 feet**. ***Hence, option C is the correct statement.***
 
• The **Sun Temple** at **Konark**, **Odisha**, was constructed in the **13th century** (around **1250 CE**) by **King Narasimhadeva I** of the **Eastern Ganga Dynasty**. It follows the **Kalinga architecture** style, which is a regional variation of the **Nagara architecture** (North Indian style), characterized by its chariot shape with **24 wheels**. ***Hence, option A is an incorrect statement.***
 
• The **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** is located in **Khajuraho**, **Madhya Pradesh**. It was built by the **Chandela rulers** between **1025** and **1050 AD**. This temple is a quintessential example of the **Nagara style** of architecture, specifically the **Central Indian** or **Panchayatana** style, known for its towering **Shikhara** that represents **Mount Kailash**. ***Hence, option B is an incorrect statement.***
 
• The **Lingaraja Temple** in **Bhubaneswar**, **Odisha**, dates back to the **11th century** and was built by **King Jajati Keshari** of the **Soma Dynasty**. It is another magnificent example of **Kalinga architecture**, featuring a massive **Vimana** (tower) and distinct sections like the **Jagamohana** (assembly hall). ***Hence, option D is an incorrect statement.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dravidian Architecture:**

 
 
• This style is primarily found in **South India**. Its defining features include a **temple enclosure** surrounded by high walls, a massive **Gopuram** (entrance gateway), and a **Vimana** (a stepped pyramid-like tower) over the **Garbhagriha** (sanctum sanctorum).
 
• Unlike North Indian temples, Dravidian temples often feature a **Temple Tank** (water reservoir) within the premises and **Prakaras** (outer corridors).
 
• Major dynasties that contributed to this style include the **Pallavas**, **Cholas**, **Pandyas**, and the **Vijayanagara Empire**.
 
 
 
• **Nagara Architecture:**
 
 
• Predominant in **North India**, this style is characterized by a curvilinear tower called the **Shikhara**.
 
• It usually lacks elaborate **boundary walls** or **gateways** (gopurams), and the entire temple is often built on a high **stone platform** (jagati).
 
• Famous examples include the **Vishvanatha Temple** in **Khajuraho** and the **Jagannath Temple** in **Puri**.
 
 
 
• **Vesara Architecture:**
 
 
• This is a **hybrid style** that combines features of both **Nagara** and **Dravidian** traditions.
 
• It was popularized by the **Chalukyas of Badami** and later the **Hoysala Empire** in the **Karnataka** region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Terminology:**

 
 
• **Garbhagriha:** The "womb-house," or the innermost sanctum where the **main deity** is placed.
 
• **Mandapa:** A pillared outdoor hall or pavilion for **public rituals** and assemblies.
 
• **Antarala:** A small **vestibule** or transition space between the **Garbhagriha** and the **Mandapa**.
 
• **Amalaka:** A stone disk with ridges on the rim, found on top of **Nagara** style **Shikharas**.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates regular elections to the board of Co-operative Societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 243ZK**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 243ZK** of the **Constitution of India** mandates the **conduct of elections** for the members of the board of a co-operative society. It ensures that elections are held before the expiry of the term of the board so that the new members can assume office immediately after the outgoing board's term ends. **Hence, this provision is central to maintaining the democratic continuity of these societies.**
 
• This article specifies that the **superintendence, direction, and control** of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections shall vest in such authority or body as may be provided by the **State Legislature** by law.
 
• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011** inserted **Part IXB** into the Constitution, which covers **Articles 243ZH to 243ZT**, specifically dealing with **Co-operative Societies**.
 
• Under these provisions, the **term of office** of the elected members of the board and its office bearers is fixed at **5 years** from the date of the election.
 
• The primary **function** of **Article 243ZK** is to prevent the prolonged administration of co-operative societies by nominated members or administrators, thereby promoting **autonomous and professional management**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 243ZI:** This article provides for the **incorporation of co-operative societies** based on the principles of voluntary formation, democratic member control, and member economic participation. It gives the state the power to make laws regarding the **incorporation, regulation, and winding up** of such societies.
 
• **Article 243ZJ:** It dictates the **number and term of members of the board**. It stipulates that the maximum number of directors in a co-operative society shall not exceed **twenty-one (21)**. It also mandates the reservation of **one seat for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes** and **two seats for women** on the board of every co-operative society having individuals as members.
 
• **Article 243ZL:** This article deals with the **supersession and suspension of the board** and interim management. It states that no board shall be superseded or kept under suspension for a period exceeding **six months**. In the case of co-operative banks, this period is specifically regulated in consultation with the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• **Article 19(1)(c):** The **97th Amendment** also modified **Article 19** to include the right to form **co-operative societies** as a **Fundamental Right** for all citizens of India.
 
• **Article 43B:** This is a **Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP)** inserted by the same amendment, which charges the **State** with the responsibility to promote **voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, and democratic control** of co-operative societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Status:** In a landmark judgment in **July 2021**, the **Supreme Court of India** struck down certain parts of the **97th Amendment**. The court held that the amendment required **ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures** under **Article 368(2)** because "Co-operative Societies" is a **State Subject** under **Entry 32 of List II (State List)** in the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• **Application:** While the Supreme Court struck down the application of Part IXB to **State Co-operative Societies**, it upheld its validity concerning **Multi-State Co-operative Societies (MSCS)**, which fall under the **Union List (Entry 44 of List I)**.
 
• **Date of Effect:** The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act** came into force on **February 15, 2012**, aiming to revitalize these institutions which are crucial for **rural credit** and **agricultural development** in **India**.

questions.question: The least common multiple of 64, 128 and A is 4480. The difference between the maximum and minimum possible values of A is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factorize: 64 = 2⁶, 128 = 2⁷, and 4480 = 2⁷ × 5 × 7.

Since 5 and 7 are missing from 64 and 128, A must have 5 × 7 = 35.

The power of 2 in A can be anything from 0 to 7 to maintain the LCM.

Minimum A = 2⁰ × 35 = 35 and Maximum A = 2⁷ × 35 = 4480.

Difference = 4480 − 35 = 4445.

**∴ Answer = 4445**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Numbers: 64, 128, and A. Their LCM is 4480.

**Formula used:**

LCM = Product of prime factors raised to their highest powers present in the numbers.

 Range of possible values for A 
• Min A = 35 (2⁰ × 5 × 7) Max A = 4480 (2⁷ × 5 × 7) A = 35 × 2x (0 ≤ x ≤ 7)

**Calculations:**

Factorizing the given numbers and LCM:

⇒ 64 = 2⁶

⇒ 128 = 2⁷

⇒ 4480 = 448 × 10 = 128 × 35 = 2⁷ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ Let A = 2x × 5y × 7z

⇒ Comparing powers in LCM(2⁶, 2⁷, A): Max(6, 7, x) = 7 ⇒ 0 ≤ x ≤ 7

⇒ Max(0, 0, y) = 1 ⇒ y = 1; Max(0, 0, z) = 1 ⇒ z = 1

⇒ Possible values of A = 2x × 35, where x ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}

⇒ Maximum A = 2⁷ × 35 = 128 × 35 = 4480

⇒ Minimum A = 2⁰ × 35 = 1 × 35 = 35

⇒ Difference = 4480 − 35 = 4445

**∴ The correct answer is 4445.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b). Note that this property does not directly apply to three or more numbers.

LCM of Fractions

The LCM of a set of fractions is calculated as: LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators.

HCF of Fractions

The HCF of a set of fractions is calculated as: HCF of numerators ÷ LCM of denominators.

Successive Division Method

HCF can be found by dividing the larger number by the smaller one and repeating the process with the remainder as the new divisor until the remainder is zero.

 Expression Breakdown 16% of 50 8 − 4/5 × 9 × 5 36

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mayilattam**, literally meaning the **Peacock Dance**, is a traditional and religious folk dance performed in the states of **Tamil Nadu** and **Kerala**.
 
• It is an artistic dance dedicated to **Lord Subrahmanya**, also known as **Lord Murugan**, who is often depicted riding a **peacock** (his vahana).
 
• The dance is typically performed by **female dancers** who dress in elaborate costumes designed to resemble a peacock, complete with a **beak** and feathers that can be manipulated to open and close like a real peacock's **plumage**.
 
• Performance of **Mayilattam** is a common sight during major **Hindu festivals** such as **Arudra Darisanam**, **Karthigai Deepam**, and the harvest festival of **Pongal**.
 
• The dancers often perform on **tall stilts** (about **10 to 12 inches** high) attached to their feet, which requires immense balance and skill to mimic the graceful movements and gait of the bird.
 
• This dance form is accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the **Nagaswaram** and **Thavil**, providing a rhythmic and energetic background to the ritualistic performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Folk Dances of Tamil Nadu:**

 
 
• **Karagattam**: An ancient folk dance where performers balance a **pot** (Karagam) on their heads while dancing. It is believed to have originated in the **Thanjavur** and **Madurai** regions.
 
• **Kavadi Attam**: A ceremonial sacrifice and dance performed by devotees during the worship of **Lord Murugan**, often involving the carrying of a decorated wooden arch called a **Kavadi**.
 
• **Kummi**: One of the oldest folk dances of **Tamil Nadu**, performed by women in a circle, clapping their hands in rhythm.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dances of Karnataka:**
 
 
• **Yakshagana**: A traditional theatre form that combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques with a unique style and form. It is prevalent in the coastal districts of **Karnataka**.
 
• **Dollu Kunitha**: A popular drum dance performed by the men of the **Kuruba** community, characterized by fast movements and powerful drum beats.
 
• **Suggi Kunitha**: A harvest dance performed by the **Halakki Vokkaliga** tribes during the spring season.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dances of Maharashtra:**
 
 
• **Lavani**: A combination of traditional song and dance, which is particularly noted for its powerful rhythm and **Dholki** beats. It is the most popular folk form in **Maharashtra**.
 
• **Koli**: The dance of the fisherfolk (**Kolis**), which reflects the rhythm of the waves and the rowing of boats.
 
• **Dhangari Gaja**: Performed by the shepherds of **Solapur** to please their God **Biruba**.
 
 
 
• **Folk Dances of Telangana:**
 
 
• **Perini Sivatandavam**: An ancient dance form that originated during the **Kakatiya dynasty**. It was traditionally performed by warriors before leaving for the battlefield.
 
• **Lambadi**: A folk dance associated with the **Lambadi** tribe, reflecting their social and daily life, often performed during harvest and marriage seasons.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **Tamil Nadu**, **Bharatanatyam** is the recognized **Classical Dance** form, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and sophisticated footwork.
 
• **Mayilattam** is part of a larger group of animal-mimicry dances known as **Aatams**, which also includes **Kaalai Attam** (Bull dance), **Karadi Attam** (Bear dance), and **Aali Attam** (Demon dance).

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution obligates the State to secure equal pay for men and women doing comparable work?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 39(d)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 39(d)** of the **Constitution of India** is a specific provision under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** which mandates that the **State** shall direct its policy towards securing that there is **equal pay for equal work** for both **men and women**. ***Hence, Article 39(d) is the correct option.***
 
• This article aims to promote **gender equality** and economic justice by ensuring that **remuneration** is based on the nature of work rather than the gender of the person performing it.
 
• While **DPSPs** are **non-justiciable** (not enforceable by any court), **Article 37** declares them **fundamental in the governance** of the country, making it the duty of the **State** to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• The principle of **equal pay for equal work** has been further strengthened by the **Supreme Court of India** in various judgments, such as **Randhir Singh vs Union of India (1982)**, where the court held that although it is not a **Fundamental Right**, it is a **Constitutional goal** under **Articles 14, 16, and 39(d)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 47**: This article states that the **State** shall regard the raising of the **level of nutrition** and the **standard of living** of its people and the **improvement of public health** as among its primary duties. It also directs the State to bring about **prohibition** of the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs. ***Hence, Article 47(a) is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 42**: It requires the **State** to make provisions for securing **just and humane conditions of work** and for **maternity relief**. It focuses on the environment and well-being of workers rather than specific wage parity between genders. ***Hence, Article 42 is incorrect.***
 
• **Article 38(1)**: This article directs the **State** to strive to promote the **welfare of the people** by securing and protecting a **social order** in which **justice** (social, economic, and political) shall inform all the institutions of national life. ***Hence, Article 38(1) is incorrect.***
 
• **Equal Remuneration Act, 1976**: To give effect to the constitutional provision of **Article 39(d)**, the **Parliament** enacted this law. It provides for the payment of **equal remuneration** to **men and women workers** and prevents **discrimination** on the ground of sex against women in the matter of **employment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are contained in **Part IV** of the **Constitution of India**, covering **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• These principles were borrowed from the **Irish Constitution**.
 
• **Article 39** contains other important clauses:
 
 
• **39(a)**: Right to an adequate means of **livelihood** for all citizens.
 
• **39(b)**: Distribution of **ownership and control** of material resources to subserve the **common good**.
 
• **39(c)**: Prevention of **concentration of wealth** and means of production.
 
• **39(e)**: Protection of the **health and strength of workers** and the tender age of children.
 
 
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** described the **DPSPs** as "**Novel Features**" of the **Indian Constitution**.

The given expression 4 cot A sec A + 3 becomes 4 cosec A + 3.

Substitute the given value cosec A = 5/4 into the simplified expression.

Result = 4 × (5/4) + 3 = 5 + 3 = 8.

**∴ Answer = 8**

cosec A = 5/4

cosec A = Hypotenuse (H) ÷ Perpendicular (P)

cot A = Base (B) ÷ Perpendicular (P)

sec A = Hypotenuse (H) ÷ Base (B)

Pythagoras Theorem: H² = P² + B²

 
 
•

 Right Triangle (3-4-5 Triplet)

questions.question: As of December 2025, under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), what is the minimum size required for a house unit provided to beneficiaries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 sq. m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G)** was launched by the **Prime Minister** on **20th November 2016**, with the primary objective of providing "Housing for All" in rural areas.
 
• Under **PMAY-G**, the minimum size of the house unit has been increased to **25 sq. m** (from **20 sq. m** under the previous **Indira Awaas Yojana**). This ensures that beneficiaries have a more spacious and dignified living environment. **Hence, the statement regarding the minimum size requirement is correct.**
 
• The house unit must include a dedicated area for **hygienic cooking**, which is a critical feature aimed at improving the health and well-being of the rural poor. **Hence, this feature is a mandatory requirement for the construction.**
 
• The scheme provides financial assistance of **Rs. 1,20,000** in **plain areas** and **Rs. 1,30,000** in **hilly states, difficult areas, and Integrated Action Plan (IAP) districts**.
 
• The **Ministry of Rural Development** is the nodal ministry responsible for the implementation and monitoring of this flagship program across the **country**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Identification of Beneficiaries**: The selection of beneficiaries is based on the housing deficiency parameters as per the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011** data, which is further validated by the **Gram Sabha** to ensure transparency.
 
• **Funding Pattern**: The cost of the assistance is shared between the **Central Government** and **State Governments** in a ratio of **60:40** in plain areas and **90:10** for **North-Eastern** and **Himalayan States**. In **Union Territories** (including **Ladakh**), the **Centre** provides **100%** of the funds.
 
• **Convergence with Other Schemes**: Beneficiaries are also entitled to **Rs. 12,000** for the construction of toilets through **Swachh Bharat Mission – Gramin (SBM-G)** or **MGNREGA**. Additionally, they receive support for **90 to 95 days** of unskilled labor wages under **MGNREGA** for the construction of their house.
 
• **Scheme Extension**: In **August 2024**, the **Union Cabinet** approved the continuation of **PMAY-G** from **FY 2024-25** to **2028-29** for the construction of an additional **2 crore houses** to cover the remaining eligible households.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monitoring through Technology**: The progress of construction is monitored through a web-based portal called **AwaasSoft** and a mobile application named **AwaasApp**. Geo-tagged photographs of different stages of construction are uploaded to ensure transparency and timely release of installments.
 
• **Landless Beneficiaries**: The **Government of India** has specific guidelines to provide land or financial assistance for purchasing land to those eligible beneficiaries who are **landless**, ensuring that the poorest of the poor are not left out.
 
• **Impact and Scale**: Since its inception in **2016**, millions of houses have been completed, significantly reducing the housing gap in rural **India** and boosting the local economy by creating demand for construction materials and labor.
